facts.claim: "Best of Anything" is track 2 on Perpetual Groove's four-track Familiar Stare, released August 16, 2016. It runs 6:44.
The Familiar Stare credits list Adam Perry (bass, vocals), Albert Suttle (drums), Brock Butler (guitar, vocals) and Matthew McDonald (keys, vocals).
On the track page for "Best of Anything", Matthew McDonald's instrument is listed as Rhodes (electric piano) and vocals.
Tom Lewis produced and mastered the Familiar Stare EP.
Songwriting credits for the track go to all four band members: Matthew McDonald, Brock Butler, Adam Perry and Albert Suttle.
The EP was recorded at Studio 1093 and Chase Park Transduction, both in Athens, GA. Artwork is by KC Cowan.

Familiar Stare has four tracks: studio recordings of two new songs and two older songs. It was the band's first non-single release of new music with the Butler/McDonald/Perry/Suttle lineup since 2007's LIVELOVEDIE.
The release is listed under the label Perpetual Groove (℗ 2016 Perpetual Groove). The band's Bandcamp page calls it their most recent studio effort.

Perpetual Groove formed in 1997. Drummer Albert Suttle and keyboardist Matt McDonald, then active-duty US Army members, met Butler and Perry at a Savannah open-mic night in 2001 and soon joined the band.
Albert Suttle left the band in September 2022 and his return was announced on October 1, 2025.

research.lineage: Bandcamp tags the release as jamband, post-rock, indie and electronic rock from Athens, placing it in the American jam band scene.

draft:
The walking bass on **Best of Anything** keeps moving, and nobody rushes it. Adam Perry's line strolls under a clean electric guitar that picks out chords one note at a time. Matthew McDonald's Rhodes lays down long, sustained chords, and Albert Suttle keeps a steady beat on kick, snare and closed hi-hat. Nothing jumps out of the pattern and nothing falls away. The four players lock into a moderate, flowing groove and trust it to carry the weight.

Trust is the feeling here, and it belongs to the band. Familiar Stare was the first non-single release of new music from the Brock Butler, McDonald, Perry and Suttle lineup since 2007's LIVELOVEDIE. That lineup goes back to a Savannah open-mic night in 2001, when Suttle and McDonald, then active-duty Army members, met Butler and Perry and soon joined up. The songwriting credit on this track goes to all four. You can hear that in how the parts fit. No one plays over anyone else. The guitar arpeggios leave gaps for the Rhodes to fill, and the bass walks through the space the drums leave open. It sounds like people who already know where the others will be.

The voice is clear and slightly breathy, and it sings melodic lines without hurry. The credits list Perry, Butler and McDonald on vocals, so the singing is shared territory too. The delivery matches the band's patience. It doesn't push or plead. It settles into the groove like one more instrument.

Bandcamp files the EP under jamband, post-rock, indie and electronic rock out of Athens, and both of the first two tags show up in this track. The jam band part is the conversation between players, the sense that a groove matters more than a peak. The post-rock part is the repeated arpeggio, a figure that stays put and lets you lean on it. Perpetual Groove recorded the EP in Athens, at Studio 1093 and Chase Park Transduction, with Tom Lewis producing and mastering. The sound is clean and polished, with a medium-sized room around the instruments and a smooth finish. If you want a jam band to sound loose and ragged, the polish might feel a little too careful. But here the care is part of the point. At nearly seven minutes, the track has time to let its patterns breathe instead of chasing a climax.

**Best of Anything** feels like a long exhale from four people back in the same room, and its steady walk tells you that you can relax too.
